    Ported from TauCeti (TauCeti.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.ModuleDecomposition, commit 580b6f9d5, Apache 2.0).

    A module over a path algebra is a representation of the quiver #

    A left module M over the path algebra kQ of a finite quiver carries one k-subspace for each vertex, Mᵥ = eᵥ M, and one k-linear map for each path, the action of that path. This file builds that data and proves the three facts that make it a representation of Q:

    • the vertex subspaces are an internal direct sum, M = ⨁ᵥ eᵥ M (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.isInternal_vertexComponent);
    • a path from a to b carries Mₐ into M_b and annihilates every other vertex subspace (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.ofPath_smul_mem_vertexComponent, LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.ofPath_smul_eq_zero_of_ne_of_mem_vertexComponent);
    • the resulting maps are functorial in the path (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.pathMap_nil, LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.pathMap_comp) and in the module (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexComponentMap_id, LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexComponentMap_comp), the two being compatible (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexComponentMap_comp_pathMap).

    This is the direction "module ↦ representation" of the equivalence between representations of Q and left kQ-modules; the vertex idempotents are what makes it work, and the finiteness of the vertex set is load-bearing, being what makes ∑ᵥ eᵥ = 1 a finite sum and kQ unital.

    The orientation is fixed by the later factor first product of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.pathAlgebra: with it, e_b · p = p and p · eₐ = p for a path p from a to b, so left multiplication by p sends the component at the source to the component at the target, and the representations obtained here are the covariant ones. Reversing the product would transpose every statement below.

    Implementation notes #

    Only the underlying data and its functoriality are built here: no object of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep k Q (Paths Q ⥤ ModuleCat k, in LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.Representation.Basic) and no functor into it is assembled, and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.dimVector is not used. Two things are missing for that. First, QuiverRep is stated over a Field k while everything below needs only a CommSemiring k, so assembling the functor here would either restrict the results or duplicate them. Second, the assembly is the roadmap target quiverRepEquivalence itself, of which this file is the object-and-morphism half.

    Main definitions #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexComponent k M v: the k-subspace eᵥ M of a kQ-module M.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.pathMap k M p: the k-linear map Mₐ → M_b given by the action of a path p from a to b.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexComponentMap k f v: the restriction of a kQ-linear map to the components at v.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexProjection k M v: the projection x ↦ eᵥ • x of M onto its component at v, the decomposition M = ⨁ᵥ eᵥ M read one vertex at a time.

    Main results #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.sum_coe_vertexProjection: the vertex projections of x sum back to x, the vertex idempotents summing to 1.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.isInternal_vertexComponent: M = ⨁ᵥ eᵥ M, with LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.coe_ofBijective_coeLinearMap_symm_apply_vertexComponent reading off the component of x at v as eᵥ • x.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.finrank_eq_sum_finrank_vertexComponent: for a kQ-module finite-dimensional over a field k, the dimension of M is the sum of the dimensions of the vertex subspaces — the total dimension read off the dimension vector.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.pathMap_nil and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.pathMap_comp: the path maps are functorial, the trivial path acting as the identity and a concatenation as the composite.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexComponentMap_comp_pathMap: the path maps are natural in the module.

    References #

    Layer 1 of TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/QuiverRepresentations/README.md, whose quiverRepEquivalence "sends a module M to the representation v ↦ eᵥ M, with an arrow acting by left multiplication, and inverts through the idempotent decomposition M = ⨁ᵥ eᵥ M (available because ∑ᵥ eᵥ = 1, hence the finiteness of the vertex set is load-bearing here)".

    The equivalence itself is classical; see Assem--Simson--Skowroński, Elements of the Representation Theory of Associative Algebras I, Ch. III, or Schiffler, Quiver Representations, Ch. 5.

    The vertex component eᵥ M of a module over the path algebra: the k-subspace on which the vertex idempotent at v acts as the identity. It is the value at v of the representation of Q attached to M.
